members.cc5IntentAnchor: Closed CC-5 intent opens 'Length prefix 0'. Verbatim at control-protocol-contract.v2 $.hostileDualChannelConformance.classes[4].intent.
members.refusalRuleAnchor: $.transportAndFraming.framing.bounds.preHandshake: 'N ... equal to 0 is refusal family RF-2, detected from the prefix alone; the receiver must refuse without buffering the body.'
members.unauthoredBodyIsForced: Correct. N=0 declares a zero-byte body, so no body exists to author.

members.cc5IntentAnchor: Closed CC-5 intent enumerates 'prefix exactly at, one over, and far over the operative bound (pre- and post-handshake bounds separately)'. 'one over' is present verbatim, and the parenthetical expressly authorizes treating the pre-handshake bound separately.
members.refusalRuleAnchor: $.transportAndFraming.framing.bounds.preHandshake: 'Until helloAck is accepted, N greater than 65536 ... is refusal family RF-2, detected from the prefix alone; the receiver must refuse without buffering the body.'
members.arithmeticCheck: The pre-handshake rule refuses N strictly greater than 65536. 65536 is therefore the last accepted value and the operative bound; 65537 is the first refused value, i.e. exactly one over. 0x00010001 = 65537. Correct.
members.absentBodyIsForced: Correct and load-bearing. The pass property is that the receiver refuses from the prefix alone without buffering the body. Authoring 65537 body bytes would contradict the property under test. A prefix-only injection is the construction the closed clause requires, not an authoring shortcut.

decision.rationale: Custody holds exactly: the subject reproduces the dispatch's expected 0c2084b1… at mode 0444 from first to last check, both named fixtures reproduce their expected digests at mode 0444, HEAD did not move, and file 08 and the coordinator record are untouched. Twenty-two dispatch attacks and fifteen further independent attacks were run; none landed. All 24 cited path/digest occurrences across 23 files reproduce, all three cited commits resolve to their claimed recordings, and all eleven recited third-party verdicts match their live files. The decisive question was whether v4 genuinely lands G21FXV3-M1 or relabels the same defect. It lands it. The offending non-object-top-level member is gone from the catalog and from disk; the replacement, a four-octet big-endian 65537 with no body, is verbatim inside the closed CC-5 intent's 'one over ... the operative bound' with its own parenthetical authorizing the pre-handshake case treated separately; and the subject converts the finding's reasoning into an explicit standing rule that RF-2 membership does not confer CC-5 membership. The secondary v3 attack is cured rather than relocated, because bound-plus-one admits exactly one value where 'non-object top level' admitted many. Both payloads were decoded from raw bytes independently of the catalog and are correct, and the absence of a body on the oversize member is required by the pass property rather than a shortcut. Two advisories and two observations are recorded; each concerns ledger phrasing or a non-normative quotation boundary, none states a false standing, and none is a bar.
